actions.name: Spark trim
actions.meaning: Degrees added to or removed from baseline spark timing.

actions.name: Lambda trim
actions.meaning: A trim to the baseline air-fuel equivalence ratio; lambda 1 is stoichiometric.

actions.name: MAP trim
actions.meaning: A pressure offset requested by the supervisor; the torque loop and compressor envelope still constrain manifold pressure.

actions.name: Radiator fan duty
actions.meaning: Absolute fan duty from zero to one, not a trim to the ECU fan command.

actions.name: Coolant pump duty
actions.meaning: Absolute pump duty from its 0.3 lower bound to full duty, not a trim.

observations.name: Engine speed
observations.meaning: Crankshaft revolutions per minute, centred around 3000 rpm.

observations.name: Manifold pressure
observations.meaning: Absolute pressure in the intake manifold after the throttle.

observations.name: Throttle proxy
observations.meaning: A model proxy based on achieved manifold pressure, not a measured throttle-position channel.

observations.name: Spark timing
observations.meaning: Actual model spark timing after the supervisory trim is added to the baseline schedule and clipped to ECU limits.

observations.name: Lambda
observations.meaning: Actual modelled air-fuel equivalence ratio relative to stoichiometric mixture.

observations.name: Block and coolant temperature
observations.meaning: Temperature of the lumped block/coolant node.

observations.name: Oil temperature
observations.meaning: Temperature of the lumped sump and oil-gallery node.

observations.name: Turbine housing temperature
observations.meaning: Modelled temperature of the turbine housing and exhaust manifold; the car has no sensor for it.

observations.name: Charge temperature
observations.meaning: Modelled intake charge temperature after compression and charge cooling.

observations.name: Ambient temperature
observations.meaning: Scenario air temperature used by vehicle, engine and thermal calculations.

observations.name: Barometric pressure
observations.meaning: Scenario pressure input in observation slot 10. It affects ambient density used by Vehicle.demand for road load.

observations.name: Specific humidity input
observations.meaning: Specific humidity supplied by the generated road scenario; this is not relative humidity.

observations.name: Vehicle speed
observations.meaning: Vehicle road speed, distinct from engine RPM.

observations.name: Current road grade
observations.meaning: The slope under the car now; it remains visible to the blinded policy.

observations.name: Grade preview at 2 s
observations.meaning: Road grade sampled two seconds ahead.

observations.name: Grade preview at 5 s
observations.meaning: Road grade sampled five seconds ahead.

observations.name: Grade preview at 15 s
observations.meaning: Road grade sampled fifteen seconds ahead.

observations.name: Grade preview at 30 s
observations.meaning: Road grade sampled thirty seconds ahead.

observations.name: Requested engine torque
observations.meaning: The torque request inferred from road load and the vehicle model.

observations.name: Driver demand change
observations.meaning: A normalized proxy for how quickly vehicle speed is changing.

observations.name: Tracking preference
observations.meaning: Episode weight on requested-torque tracking, drawn uniformly from 0.45 to 0.70.

observations.name: Fuel preference
observations.scale: First of two Dirichlet(1,1) shares of remaining weight
observations.meaning: Episode preference share for fuel saving after the tracking floor is set.

observations.name: Component-life preference
observations.scale: Second of two Dirichlet(1,1) shares of remaining weight
observations.meaning: Episode preference share for modeled damage reduction after the tracking floor is set.

concepts.name: Reference torque PI loop
concepts.meaning: The parallel baseline torque PI loop produces its own absolute manifold pressure with zero supervisory MAP trim. The reference is not supervised pressure minus its trim.
concepts.why: It identifies the parallel reference pressure for the same torque request.
concepts.caveat: Reference pressure is exported by the model, not measured vehicle ECU output.

concepts.name: Four-stroke cycle
concepts.meaning: Each cylinder completes intake, compression, power and exhaust over two crankshaft revolutions.
concepts.why: It connects piston motion to how engine speed becomes repeated combustion work.
concepts.range: One cylinder from intake-valve closing through exhaust-valve opening.
concepts.increase: More trapped charge can increase work and exhaust energy.
concepts.decrease: Less trapped charge reduces available work.
concepts.caveat: A single-zone 0-D calculation, not a full 3-D flow simulation.
concepts.evidence_note: The model advances cylinder pressure in small crank-angle increments over one firing cycle.

concepts.name: B58 engine geometry
concepts.meaning: The represented engine is a 2,997.5 cc inline-six B58B30O1 with an 82.0 mm bore and 94.6 mm stroke.
concepts.why: Bore, stroke, cylinder count and compression ratio set volume, air capacity and pressure-work scaling.
concepts.range: Model geometry: 2,997.5 cc, six cylinders, 10.2:1 compression ratio.
concepts.increase: More displacement can ingest more air per cycle at the same manifold conditions.
concepts.decrease: Smaller displacement reduces air and fuel per cycle.
concepts.caveat: This is the project model identity and geometry, not OEM-certified calibration or CAD.
concepts.evidence_note: Geometry defaults are defined in plant.Geometry and b58() names the 2023 Supra 3.0 engine.

concepts.name: Turbocharger
concepts.meaning: Exhaust energy spins a turbine connected to a compressor that raises intake pressure.
concepts.why: Boost increases trapped air, torque potential and the heat carried into the exhaust system.
concepts.range: The scenario runs near 175 kPa manifold pressure; the compressor ceiling depends on air flow.
concepts.increase: More boost can raise engine torque and exhaust enthalpy, subject to the compressor map.
concepts.decrease: Less boost lowers trapped air and may limit torque delivery.
concepts.caveat: Compressor/turbine are simplified closures, not a detailed turbo map transient model.
concepts.evidence_note: The compressor ceiling uses a log-informed envelope; compressor and turbine transient dynamics are simplified.

concepts.name: Air charge and airflow
concepts.meaning: Manifold pressure, charge temperature, RPM and volumetric efficiency determine the air trapped each cycle.
concepts.why: Combustion cannot release more fuel energy than the available oxygen supports.
concepts.range: Operating envelope is informed by logged airflow and pressure; high-flow MAF saturates above about 0.314 kg/s.
concepts.increase: More air can support more fuel and torque when mixture and knock constraints permit.
concepts.decrease: Less air reduces torque capacity.
concepts.caveat: The OBD intake-temperature channel is upstream of the charge cooler; it is not charge temperature.
concepts.evidence_note: The model calculates trapped air mass and passes airflow into its compressor-ceiling calculation.

concepts.name: Charge temperature
concepts.meaning: Compressed intake air heats up; the model estimates the charge temperature using ambient and engine thermal state.
concepts.why: Hotter charge is less dense and can increase knock tendency.
concepts.range: Modelled state; not directly measured at the manifold in the project logs.
concepts.increase: At fixed pressure, hotter air is less dense and generally increases knock risk.
concepts.decrease: Cooling the charge raises density and knock margin.
concepts.caveat: Intercooler behavior is represented by an empirical correction.
concepts.evidence_note: engine_env computes charge_temperature before the cycle prediction.

concepts.name: Combustion
concepts.meaning: A Wiebe burn-progress curve releases mixture energy over crank angle while a single-zone first-law balance updates cylinder pressure and temperature.
concepts.why: The combustion calculation supplies torque, fuel use, exhaust temperature and knock exposure.
concepts.range: One idealized cycle per environment step.
concepts.increase: More released energy can increase indicated work and exhaust temperature.
concepts.decrease: Slow or incomplete burning reduces useful work and can raise unburned fuel losses.
concepts.caveat: It does not resolve cylinder-to-cylinder variation or 3-D flame propagation.
concepts.evidence_note: run_cycle integrates pressure and temperature through the modeled burn.

concepts.name: Fuel mass flow
concepts.meaning: Fuel mass flow is calculated from trapped air mass, engine speed and the modeled lambda value.
concepts.why: Fuel affects torque, consumption, exhaust mass and thermal loading.
concepts.range: Lambda is clipped to 0.70–1.25 by the environment.
concepts.increase: More fuel can add energy but raises fuel use and exhaust mass.
concepts.decrease: Less fuel can reduce consumption but may reduce torque or alter combustion temperature.
concepts.caveat: The project does not infer production ECU fuel commands from an OEM calibration map.
concepts.evidence_note: plant.py calculates fuel and air mass flow from per-cylinder trapped mass and RPM.

concepts.name: Actual spark timing
concepts.meaning: Actual model spark timing equals the baseline schedule plus the applied supervisory spark trim, then clipped to ECU limits.
concepts.why: Timing changes work, exhaust temperature, fuel use and knock exposure together.
concepts.range: Trim action: −8 to +4 deg; total spark is separately clipped to ECU limits.
concepts.increase: Advance can increase efficiency and torque until knock risk rises.
concepts.decrease: Retard generally reduces knock risk but can increase exhaust temperature and fuel use.
concepts.caveat: This refers to actual trimmed timing, not the baseline schedule alone.
concepts.evidence_note: engine_env adds the action trim to BaselineECU spark and clips to ECU limits.

concepts.name: Knock integral
concepts.meaning: The Douaud–Eyzat model accumulates end-gas autoignition exposure during the unburned part of combustion.
concepts.why: It supplies a knock-risk estimate and a quadratic contribution to the simulated damage proxy above its knee.
concepts.range: The selected knee is 0.85; model realism has not been validated on this car.
concepts.increase: Higher integral increases the modelled probability and knock damage term.
concepts.decrease: Retarding spark or reducing load generally lowers predicted exposure.
concepts.caveat: Knock is an unvalidated model estimate and the largest unresolved assumption behind apparent protection margins.
concepts.evidence_note: plant.py integrates crank-angle exposure; engine_env.damage_rate adds a penalty above 0.85.

concepts.name: Engine torque
concepts.meaning: Cylinder pressure work minus estimated friction and pumping work gives brake torque.
concepts.why: The vehicle model must deliver road-load torque while the controller manages fuel and component temperatures.
concepts.range: Geometry and calibrated operating envelope determine feasible output.
concepts.increase: More delivered torque reduces demand-tracking error.
concepts.decrease: Insufficient torque raises tracking cost and can make a controller appear protective by starving demand.
concepts.caveat: This is simulated torque, not a dynamometer validation result.
concepts.evidence_note: plant.py converts net BMEP and total displacement to torque.

concepts.name: Road load and torque request
concepts.meaning: Speed, acceleration, grade, air density, rolling resistance and drag determine wheel force; gearing maps it to engine torque request.
concepts.why: A fair protection comparison must retain the driver's requested road performance.
concepts.range: Locked result scenario: 12% grade at 130 km/h, 42 C ambient.
concepts.increase: Steeper grade or higher speed raises road load and requested power.
concepts.decrease: Lower road load reduces required wheel force and engine torque.
concepts.caveat: A 130 km/h, 12% climb is a synthetic binding scenario, not a road the car logged.
concepts.evidence_note: Vehicle.demand computes vehicle force and engine request; tracking reward penalizes unmet torque.

concepts.name: ZF 8HP51 gearbox
concepts.meaning: Eight gear ratios and a final drive convert wheel speed and torque into engine RPM and torque demand.
concepts.why: Gear selection sets engine operating point, per-cycle load and exhaust heating.
concepts.range: Eight forward ratios; locked climb holds seventh gear in the reported scenario.
concepts.increase: A numerically higher ratio raises engine speed for fixed wheel speed.
concepts.decrease: A taller ratio lowers RPM but raises torque required per engine cycle.
concepts.caveat: Shift logic is simplified relative to the vehicle's production transmission controller.
concepts.evidence_note: Vehicle defines the eight ratios and demand logic, including kickdown when torque cannot be delivered.

concepts.name: Exhaust mass flow
concepts.meaning: The turbine gas stream is air mass plus fuel mass leaving the cylinders.
concepts.why: Exhaust mass flow controls modeled turbine-side heat transfer.
concepts.range: Flow varies with load, mixture and engine speed.
concepts.increase: More exhaust mass strengthens gas-to-housing heat transfer at a given temperature difference.
concepts.decrease: Lower flow weakens modeled gas-side transfer.
concepts.caveat: Gas temperature and turbine flow use simplified exhaust-system closures.
concepts.evidence_note: engine_env sends mdot_air + mdot_fuel to the thermal network.

concepts.name: Exhaust gas temperature
concepts.meaning: The cycle estimates exhaust temperature after blowdown and an empirical port/runner heat-loss step.
concepts.why: Exhaust is the principal heat source for the turbine housing model.
concepts.range: Modelled; no turbine inlet thermocouple is available in the logged data.
concepts.increase: Hotter exhaust raises turbine heat input when the housing is cooler than gas.
concepts.decrease: Cooler exhaust lowers turbine heating, all else equal.
concepts.caveat: The port heat-loss coefficient is empirical and EGT max is outside one validation band.
concepts.evidence_note: plant.py uses an empirical UA_PORT and computes exhaust temperature from end-of-expansion conditions.

concepts.name: Block and coolant thermal node
concepts.meaning: The lumped block/coolant state receives fuel energy, exchanges heat with oil according to their temperature difference, and rejects heat to ambient air and the radiator through a surrogate thermostat.
concepts.why: Thermal memory means a short grade change can affect later temperatures and damage.
concepts.range: Node initialized warm at 363 K; explicit Euler integration is numerically stiff at the scenario timestep.
concepts.increase: More heat input raises block temperature until heat rejection balances it.
concepts.decrease: More radiator/ambient heat rejection lowers block temperature.
concepts.caveat: The block/coolant update oscillates at dt=1 s. Do not quote H/τ sweep results until the numerical integration is corrected.
concepts.evidence_note: ThermalNetwork has separate block, oil and turbine states; block/oil parameters are derived from available logs.

concepts.name: Oil thermal node
concepts.meaning: The lumped sump and galleries state receives engine-speed and fuel-energy heating, exchanges heat with the block according to their temperature difference, and exchanges heat with ambient air according to road speed.
concepts.why: Oil temperature contributes to the project’s thermal damage proxy and is also available as a car log channel on some drives.
concepts.range: Validation against the measured car is limited; reported climb oil is modelled.
concepts.increase: Fuel energy and engine-speed friction and churning are direct heat sources; block/oil exchange runs from the hotter node to the colder node.
concepts.decrease: More road-speed cooling or lower engine speed lowers its equilibrium.
concepts.caveat: The block/coolant update oscillates at dt=1 s. Do not quote H/τ sweep results until corrected.
concepts.evidence_note: ThermalNetwork computes a lumped oil state; its structure is fit to seven drives but held-out drive10 underpredicts the peak by 16.9 K.

concepts.name: Turbine housing temperature
concepts.meaning: The lumped turbine housing exchanges heat with exhaust gas and ambient air, from the hotter side to the colder side; gas can cool the housing when colder. The current network has no direct fan or pump cooling of this node.
concepts.why: Its assumed time constant is central to the preview-horizon hypothesis H/tau.
concepts.range: The demonstrator uses a 1123 K damage trigger; tau is roughly tens of seconds in the current model.
concepts.increase: Higher exhaust flow or gas temperature can raise housing temperature faster.
concepts.decrease: More ambient heat rejection lowers the node toward ambient.
concepts.caveat: This is a modeled temperature using assumed turbine thermal parameters, not a measured car channel.
concepts.evidence_note: ThermalNetwork computes this state from assumed heat capacity and transfer coefficients; there is no matching vehicle sensor.

concepts.name: Damage proxy
concepts.meaning: Instantaneous proxy combines exponential turbine and oil temperature terms plus a quadratic knock excess penalty.
concepts.why: The agent’s life reward compares instantaneous damage rates; the episode score accumulates rate × dt. This is a simulation proxy, not measured component life.
concepts.range: A relative simulation metric; it is not a warranty or remaining-life estimate.
concepts.increase: Hotter nodes and knock-integral excess increase accumulated proxy damage.
concepts.decrease: Lower modelled temperatures or knock integral lower the proxy.
concepts.caveat: No empirical mapping from these units to real component lifespan is established.
concepts.evidence_note: The sole damage_rate function is in engine_env.py; 1123 K and 408 K are its temperature knees.

concepts.name: Future grade preview
concepts.meaning: The sighted agent receives future road grade at 2, 5, 15 and 30 seconds; the blind arm gets zeros in only those four slots.
concepts.why: The experiment isolates whether future-grade information adds value beyond current grade and thermal state.
concepts.range: H=2–30 s; current H/tau point is approximate and does not establish a curve.
concepts.increase: A preview signal can let the controller act before the car reaches a grade change.
concepts.decrease: Blinding zeroes the future-grade slots but does not hide the current grade.
concepts.caveat: Preview is information from a generated road profile, not an external map or a real-time vehicle feed.
concepts.evidence_note: _preview samples PREVIEW_S; _obs includes current grade for both arms.

concepts.name: Baseline ECU reference
concepts.meaning: A production-representative model schedules spark, lambda, knock response and fan; a parallel thermal state supplies the reference.
concepts.why: Fuel and component-life reward terms compare the supervised engine against this baseline.
concepts.range: It is not extracted factory firmware or a tuned ECU binary.
concepts.increase: The reference defines the no-supervisor trajectory for a paired comparison.
concepts.decrease: An inaccurate reference can bias every relative reward and damage comparison.
concepts.caveat: Call it production-representative, never the vehicle’s actual ECU code.
concepts.evidence_note: BaselineECU and thermal_base run beside the supervised environment.

concepts.name: Normalized policy output
concepts.meaning: The SAC policy emits five values in [−1, 1]; the environment rescales them to action-specific units, slew-limits them, and clips to bounds.
concepts.why: A shared network output range can control signals with different engineering units.
concepts.range: Five channels; SLEW scales with dt.
concepts.increase: Increasing an action output moves each actuator toward its high bound.
concepts.decrease: Decreasing moves it toward its low bound.
concepts.caveat: Fan and pump are absolute duties; a zero normalized output is not a universal neutral action.
concepts.evidence_note: ACT_LO, ACT_HI and SLEW define conversion and per-second movement limits.

concepts.name: Fuel reward term
concepts.meaning: Fuel reward is the fractional reduction in fuel flow against the parallel baseline for that step.
concepts.why: It rewards efficiency without using an absolute fuel-scale coefficient.
concepts.range: Positive means the supervised model uses less fuel than its baseline at that step.
concepts.increase: Lower agent fuel flow raises this term.
concepts.decrease: Higher agent fuel flow lowers it.
concepts.caveat: The episode preference weight changes how much this term matters.
concepts.evidence_note: r_fuel = (baseline fuel − fuel) / (baseline fuel + 1e−6).

concepts.name: Component-life reward term
concepts.meaning: Life reward is the baseline-relative reduction in modelled damage rate with a small denominator stabilizer.
concepts.why: It encourages thermal and knock protection while making its model assumptions visible.
concepts.range: Positive means the agent’s damage proxy is lower than the baseline’s.
concepts.increase: Lower agent damage proxy raises the term.
concepts.decrease: Higher modeled damage lowers it.
concepts.caveat: The proxy is not measured component life, and reward weights can trade it against fuel.
concepts.evidence_note: r_life = (baseline damage_rate − damage_rate) / (baseline damage_rate + 0.05).

concepts.name: Torque tracking reward
concepts.meaning: A negative error term penalizes failure to deliver requested engine torque, with a steeper penalty beyond 5% error.
concepts.why: Without it an agent could appear protective by withholding torque.
concepts.range: 5% tolerance before the additional hinge penalty.
concepts.increase: Smaller torque error makes the negative penalty less severe.
concepts.decrease: More unmet torque makes the reward more negative.
concepts.caveat: Returned torque, knock and EGT costs are diagnostics; they are not additional reward terms here.
concepts.evidence_note: r_resp uses normalized absolute torque error and TRACK_HINGE=25 beyond TRACK_TOL=0.05.

concepts.name: Preference-weighted reward
concepts.meaning: Reward combines tracking, fuel and life terms with episode-specific preference weights, uncertainty and actuator smoothness.
concepts.why: One trained policy can express different trade-offs across preference settings.
concepts.range: Weights are resampled for each episode; they are not safety guarantees.
concepts.increase: The policy favors whichever positive weighted improvements dominate for that episode.
concepts.decrease: Unmet torque, uncertainty or abrupt actuator motion lowers reward.
concepts.caveat: Low life preference can permit an agent to perform worse than baseline on some episodes.
concepts.evidence_note: The reward formula uses w[0] tracking, w[1] fuel, and w[2] life.

concepts.name: Constraint diagnostics
concepts.meaning: The environment reports torque shortfall, knock event and high-EGT costs in info as diagnostics.
concepts.why: They expose unsafe-looking behavior even where the scalar preference reward can trade objectives.
concepts.range: Torque tolerance 3% for this diagnostic; knock threshold KI>1; EGT reference 1223 K.
concepts.increase: More shortfall, knock threshold exceedances or high EGT increase costs.
concepts.decrease: Meeting torque and staying below modeled thresholds reduces them.
concepts.caveat: These costs are not a hard safety shield and are not all subtracted from reward.
concepts.evidence_note: cost_torque, cost_knock and cost_egt are calculated after the reward and returned in info.

concepts.name: Thermal time constant
concepts.meaning: For a lumped node, heat capacity divided by heat-transfer rate gives the approximate response time to a step change.
concepts.why: The hypothesis compares this response time tau with how far ahead grade information arrives H.
concepts.range: Modelled turbine tau is about 47 seconds in the locked scenario; this is not directly measured.
concepts.increase: A larger tau means the component responds more slowly to heating.
concepts.decrease: A smaller tau means temperatures respond more quickly.
concepts.caveat: Numerical stiffness in the block node currently prevents quoting the H/tau sweep.
concepts.evidence_note: thermal.py explains C/UA and identifies turbine C and UA as assumptions.

concepts.name: H over tau
concepts.meaning: H/tau is preview horizon divided by component thermal response time; it is the proposed organizing variable for preview value.
concepts.why: The project asks when acquiring future information is useful, not whether one controller wins once.
concepts.range: A single retrain scenario lies near H/tau 0.64 using an assumed turbine time constant.
concepts.increase: Larger ratio means the preview horizon is long relative to thermal response time.
concepts.decrease: Smaller ratio means preview is short relative to response time.
concepts.caveat: The universal curve is a hypothesis, not a current result.
concepts.evidence_note: The claim predicts points from different plants collapse onto one curve; no corrected cross-plant sweep has established this.

concepts.name: Current grade
concepts.meaning: The road slope at the vehicle’s current position, available to both sighted and blind policies.
concepts.why: The comparison asks what future grade adds beyond an ordinary current-state measurement.
concepts.range: The frame card reports grade in percent; observation slot 13 stores the fractional grade multiplied by 12.
concepts.increase: A steeper uphill grade increases wheel force demand.
concepts.decrease: A flatter or downhill grade lowers or reverses grade force.
concepts.caveat: Historical Phase D’s fixed road and thermal clock let the nominal blind policy infer timing.
concepts.evidence_note: Observation slot 13 is current grade; slots 14–17 alone are zeroed when preview is disabled.

concepts.name: Trained SAC supervisor
concepts.meaning: A Soft Actor-Critic policy maps 23 observations to five bounded supervisory actions.
concepts.why: The agent tests whether a learned policy can use current state and preview while balancing preferences.
concepts.range: Stored policy.npz exports are not exact scored Stable-Baselines3 final.zip artifacts.
concepts.increase: A changed observation or learned parameter can change the action.
concepts.decrease: The blind policy lacks future-grade values but retains current grade and thermal state.
concepts.caveat: Exported policy replays lack complete code identity and must be labelled UNVERIFIED, never the exact recorded scored traces.
concepts.evidence_note: Current results include ten sighted and ten blind agents, each trained for 50,000 steps on varied roads.

concepts.name: Current preview result
concepts.meaning: Across ten seed pairs, sighted-minus-blind damage-cut mean is +1.169 percentage points with 95% CI [−4.439, +6.778].
concepts.why: This is the directly relevant experiment for the incremental value of grade preview in the current retrain.
concepts.range: n=10; paired t p=0.6484, exact Wilcoxon p=0.4316.
concepts.increase: Positive sighted-minus-blind cut favors preview on this tested configuration.
concepts.decrease: Negative favors the blinded policy; an interval spanning zero leaves direction unresolved.
concepts.caveat: INCONCLUSIVE; do not say preview has no effect or that the H/tau rule is proven.
concepts.evidence_note: Generated terrain_dt1 index records paired data, confidence interval and paired tests.

concepts.name: Measured, derived and assumed quantities
concepts.meaning: Logs provide some signals; scripts derive identifiable parameters; other states and constants remain modelled or assumed.
concepts.why: A precise dashboard number is not automatically a directly measured vehicle value.
concepts.range: The turbine housing temperature and turbine time constant are modelled from assumed parameters.
concepts.increase: More independent measurements can reduce uncertainty in fitted parameters.
concepts.decrease: Using an assumed parameter as if measured overstates evidence.
concepts.caveat: Eight of eleven validation checks pass; validation is limited and not comprehensive.
concepts.evidence_note: REFERENCES.md distinguishes measured, derived, modelled and assumed values.

concepts.name: Engine speed
concepts.meaning: Crankshaft speed in revolutions per minute.
concepts.why: Speed affects cycle rate, gear mapping, airflow and friction.
concepts.evidence_note: Crankshaft speed in revolutions per minute.
concepts.increase: The effect depends on the coupled operating point; use a controlled model step to observe it.
concepts.decrease: The effect depends on the coupled operating point; use a controlled model step to observe it.

concepts.name: Manifold pressure
concepts.meaning: Absolute pressure after the throttle at the modeled intake manifold.
concepts.why: It affects trapped air together with RPM, charge temperature and volumetric efficiency.
concepts.evidence_note: Absolute pressure after the throttle at the modeled intake manifold.
concepts.increase: The effect depends on the coupled operating point; use a controlled model step to observe it.
concepts.decrease: The effect depends on the coupled operating point; use a controlled model step to observe it.

concepts.name: Throttle proxy
concepts.meaning: Normalized model proxy based on achieved manifold pressure, not a measured throttle-position channel.
concepts.why: It helps describe the current modeled load.
concepts.evidence_note: Normalized model proxy based on achieved manifold pressure, not a measured throttle-position channel.
concepts.increase: The effect depends on the coupled operating point; use a controlled model step to observe it.
concepts.decrease: The effect depends on the coupled operating point; use a controlled model step to observe it.

concepts.name: Lambda
concepts.meaning: Modeled air-fuel equivalence ratio relative to stoichiometric mixture; 1.0 is stoichiometric.
concepts.why: Mixture affects fuel mass, combustion, exhaust heat and knock.
concepts.evidence_note: Modeled air-fuel equivalence ratio relative to stoichiometric mixture; 1.0 is stoichiometric.
concepts.increase: The effect depends on the coupled operating point; use a controlled model step to observe it.
concepts.decrease: The effect depends on the coupled operating point; use a controlled model step to observe it.

concepts.name: Ambient temperature
concepts.meaning: Ambient temperature supplied by the generated scenario.
concepts.why: It affects air density and thermal heat rejection.
concepts.evidence_note: Ambient temperature supplied by the generated scenario.
concepts.increase: The effect depends on the coupled operating point; use a controlled model step to observe it.
concepts.decrease: The effect depends on the coupled operating point; use a controlled model step to observe it.

concepts.name: Barometric pressure
concepts.meaning: Scenario pressure input in observation slot 10. It affects ambient density used by Vehicle.demand for road load.
concepts.why: It connects the scenario atmosphere to road torque demand, not to air mass at fixed MAP.
concepts.evidence_note: Scenario pressure input in observation slot 10. It affects ambient density used by Vehicle.demand for road load.
concepts.increase: For fixed temperature, higher scenario pressure raises ambient density and the aerodynamic part of road demand.
concepts.decrease: For fixed temperature, lower scenario pressure lowers ambient density and the aerodynamic part of road demand.
concepts.caveat: Road generators set p_baro to 101.3 kPa; altitude is not modeled. The environment compressor ceiling does not pass p_baro and uses plant.boost_ceiling_kpa default inlet pressure 99.3 kPa.

concepts.name: Specific humidity input
concepts.meaning: The generated road stores a fixed specific-humidity field (0.012 kg water per kg dry air) and exposes its normalized value to the actor.
concepts.why: It is included in the observation vector for provenance and future experiments; the current engine/air-density equations do not use it.
concepts.evidence_note: Scenario water-vapor mass ratio (kg water per kg dry air), not relative humidity.
concepts.increase: The effect depends on the coupled operating point; use a controlled model step to observe it.
concepts.decrease: The effect depends on the coupled operating point; use a controlled model step to observe it.
concepts.caveat: The source cycle fixes this input at 0.012 kg/kg; it is not relative humidity and currently has no causal effect on modeled plant outputs.

concepts.name: Vehicle speed
concepts.meaning: Road speed supplied by the scenario trajectory.
concepts.why: Speed controls road load, gear choice and thermal heat rejection.
concepts.evidence_note: Road speed supplied by the scenario trajectory.
concepts.increase: The effect depends on the coupled operating point; use a controlled model step to observe it.
concepts.decrease: The effect depends on the coupled operating point; use a controlled model step to observe it.

concepts.name: Grade preview at 2 s
concepts.meaning: Road grade sampled two seconds ahead from the generated road.
concepts.why: It can let a controller prepare before a grade change arrives.
concepts.evidence_note: Road grade sampled two seconds ahead from the generated road.

tour.title: The road creates the load
tour.subtitle: A slope becomes engine torque demand
tour.body: Road speed, acceleration, grade and air density determine wheel force. The gearbox maps that road force to the engine operating point.
tour.experiment: Enable “Override the remaining road,” set grade from 0% to 12%, then advance 30 s. Compare requested engine torque before and after the grade change.

tour.title: Engine 101: how a cylinder makes torque
tour.subtitle: Four strokes, two crankshaft turns
tour.body: The engine turns fuel energy into heat and pressure. Intake, compression, power and exhaust take two crankshaft revolutions; pressure pushes the piston and turns the crankshaft. This project models a simplified single-zone cycle, not three-dimensional combustion.
tour.experiment: Open the Engine 101 lab and step through intake, compression, power and exhaust. Watch the piston compress the mixture before the spark starts the power stroke.

tour.title: Air and fuel make the charge
tour.subtitle: Boost raises air mass; lambda sets fuel relative to it
tour.body: The compressor supplies pressurized air. Charge temperature and engine speed determine how much oxygen enters each cycle; lambda sets fuel mass for that air.
tour.experiment: Keep the road override fixed and select the manual supervisor. Increase MAP trim slightly, advance one second, then compare MAP, modeled airflow and fuel flow.

tour.title: Spark starts a finite burn
tour.subtitle: Timing changes work, exhaust and knock together
tour.body: Spark timing sets when the plug fires before top dead centre. Changing it can alter torque, fuel use, exhaust heat and knock exposure at once; follow those effects through the cycle and test one small trim at a time.
tour.experiment: Open Engine 101 and follow intake, compression, power and exhaust. During compression the valves close and the piston squeezes the mixture; excess spark advance can raise modeled knock exposure.

tour.title: Exhaust carries heat to the turbo
tour.subtitle: Air plus fuel flow through the hot side
tour.body: Exhaust temperature and mass flow heat the turbine housing. The model remembers that heat instead of resetting temperature every step.
tour.experiment: Keep the road fixed, raise load with MAP trim, and advance 30 s. Compare modeled exhaust gas temperature with the slower turbine-housing response.

tour.title: Three nodes remember heat
tour.subtitle: Block, oil and turbine respond at different rates
tour.body: Heat capacities and transfer paths create memory. The block and oil parameters are derived from logs, while turbine dynamics remain assumed.
tour.experiment: Open Thermal memory, apply a short load change, and compare how quickly block, oil and turbine temperature states respond.

tour.title: The agent sees state and preview
tour.subtitle: Twenty-three values become five supervisory commands
tour.body: Both policies see present engine and vehicle state. Sighted agents also see four future grade samples; the blind arm receives zeroes in only those slots.
tour.experiment: Turn future-grade preview off and load/reset, then turn it on and load/reset. Compare observation slots 14–17; current grade in slot 13 remains visible in both runs.

tour.title: Reward balances competing goals
tour.subtitle: Deliver torque, save fuel, reduce modelled damage
tour.body: Episode weights change the balance among response, fuel and life proxy. Returned constraint costs help reveal bad behavior even when a scalar reward trades objectives.
tour.experiment: Open Preview comparison, choose a seed, and compare tracking, fuel and life weights and reward terms for the two actors on that fixed seed.

tour.title: What the experiment says
tour.subtitle: The preview effect remains inconclusive
tour.body: The paired interval includes zero and the tests are not significant. Agents’ apparent advantage over hand policies depends heavily on the untested knock model.
tour.experiment: Open Research result and read the paired 95% interval and both p-values. Explain why an interval spanning zero is inconclusive.

viva.question: How does an engine turn fuel into shaft torque?
viva.short: Fuel burns in the cylinder and raises pressure. The piston turns that pressure into crankshaft rotation.
viva.technical: Each cylinder completes intake, compression, power and exhaust over two crankshaft revolutions. The simplified single-zone cycle integrates pressure work and subtracts estimated friction and pumping work to produce modeled brake torque.

viva.question: Why does engine temperature have memory?
viva.short: The metal and fluids store heat, so their temperatures respond over time instead of instantly following load.
viva.technical: Each thermal node integrates heat capacity times temperature change against heat input and transfer to connected nodes and ambient. A change in load can keep affecting block, oil and turbine states after the road demand changes.

viva.question: What five levers does the supervisor actually control?
viva.short: Spark trim, lambda trim, MAP trim, radiator-fan duty and coolant-pump duty.
viva.technical: The action vector is ordered [spark, lambda, MAP, fan, pump]. Bounds are [−8,+4] degrees, [−0.15,+0.06] lambda, [−40,+15] kPa, [0,1] fan fraction and [0.3,1] pump fraction. Spark/lambda/MAP are additive trims; fan and pump are absolute duties, all subject to slew limits.

viva.question: Why is turbine-housing temperature not measured from the car?
viva.short: The logged vehicle has no turbine-housing temperature sensor, so this value is a model estimate.
viva.technical: The thermal network integrates a turbine state from exhaust energy and assumed heat capacity and transfer coefficients. It is not an OBD channel and has no direct sensor validation on this car.

viva.question: What information does future-grade preview add?
viva.short: It adds four upcoming road-grade samples at 2, 5, 15 and 30 seconds ahead.
viva.technical: The sighted policy observes current grade at slot 13 and future samples at slots 14–17. Disabling preview zeros only those four samples; the blinded policy still sees current grade.

viva.question: How does the supervisor differ from the baseline ECU?
viva.short: The baseline ECU sets its base engine commands. The supervisor reads observations and adds bounded trims while the vehicle model handles torque and gear selection.
viva.technical: BaselineECU supplies baseline spark and lambda. The policy selects five supervisory actions; a torque PI loop constrains MAP and the vehicle model selects gears. The bridge “baseline” policy is the project neutral supervisor and its fan/pump duties may not exactly match every ECU fan schedule.

viva.question: Why are fuel and life rewards measured against a baseline?
viva.short: They score savings relative to the baseline for the same episode, while torque response is scored separately.
viva.technical: r_fuel=(baseline fuel−fuel)/(baseline fuel+1e−6); r_life=(baseline damage_rate−damage_rate)/(baseline damage_rate+0.05). engine_env.py:934–946 combines r_resp, r_fuel and r_life with actual obs_in[20:23] weights and uncertainty/smoothness penalties. It is not a best-action label or independent validation. Constraint costs are diagnostics and must not be subtracted again. Missing penalties imply partial decomposition; the total stays frame.reward.

viva.question: Why does a steeper road grade raise requested engine torque?
viva.short: Gravity pulls harder against the car on a steeper climb, so the vehicle model requests more wheel force and engine torque.
viva.technical: Vehicle demand combines grade, rolling resistance, aerodynamic drag and acceleration into wheel force. Gear ratios and final drive map wheel force to engine torque demand, which enters the tracking error.

viva.question: What can spark retard do to exhaust temperature?
viva.short: Retarding spark can reduce knock risk, but it may send more heat into the exhaust and increase fuel use.
viva.technical: The cycle model changes combustion phasing and work when spark timing moves. Retard generally reduces modeled knock exposure while tending to raise exhaust temperature at the relevant high-load operating point; the direction and size depend on the operating point.

viva.question: What does lambda tell us, and what does enrichment change?
viva.short: Lambda compares the mixture with stoichiometric air-fuel ratio. Lower lambda is richer and uses more fuel per unit air.
viva.technical: Lambda is actual air-fuel ratio divided by stoichiometric ratio; λ=1 is stoichiometric and λ<1 is rich. The model uses air mass and lambda to calculate fuel mass. Enrichment can reduce knock tendency in the protection logic but raises modeled fuel flow; exhaust-temperature effects depend on the operating point.

viva.question: Why does the reward penalize missed torque?
viva.short: Without a tracking penalty, a controller could look protective by refusing to make the requested torque.
viva.technical: r_resp uses normalized absolute torque error with a hinge above TRACK_TOL=0.05 and TRACK_HINGE=25. The tracking weight is floored at 0.45; this keeps torque delivery as a requirement while fuel and life express the preference trade-off.

viva.question: What is the current preview result?
viva.short: In the current paired retrain, preview’s effect is inconclusive; the data do not show either a reliable benefit or no effect.
viva.technical: For ten sighted/blind seed pairs, the mean difference in damage cut is +1.1693 percentage points, 95% CI [−4.4391,+6.7777], paired t p=0.648406 and exact Wilcoxon p=0.431641. The interval spans zero and both tests are nonsignificant. In the separate hand-policy premise, predictive is 0.32 points worse than current-grade.

viva.question: What does H/τ mean, and is the curve established?
viva.short: H/τ compares preview time with thermal response time. The corrected cross-plant curve is not established yet.
viva.technical: H is a preview horizon and τ=C/UA is a thermal time constant. Turbine heat capacity remains assumed, and the current thermal update oscillates at dt=1 s; the sweep at dt=2 s is not quotable until integration is corrected and the agreed preregistered experiment is run.

viva.question: What makes a trained actor replay the exact scored result?
viva.short: The exported weights alone are not enough; the model and code identity must also match the scored run.
viva.technical: The current exports provide policy.npz weights and data_sha1 but no plant_sha or scored final.zip hash. The generated score summaries are available, but raw eval_record.npz and train_record.npz are machine-local/gitignored; live actor runs are UNVERIFIED reenactments, not exact scored traces.

viva.question: If we only predict temperature, who chooses spark and fan?
viva.short: A controller chooses actions; forecasting alone does not.
viva.technical: SAC maps obs_in to five actions. Engine and thermal models calculate outcomes. Sequential decisions depend on state, thermal memory and cumulative reward. MPC and imitation are alternatives; no superiority is established without comparison. Training updates weights separately; this app reuses frozen weights or manual/hand-written policies.

viva.question: Does 12% lower damage index mean 12% longer component life?
viva.short: No. It is a relative thermal/knock index, not measured lifetime.
viva.technical: engine_env.py:636 combines exponential turbine/oil temperatures and optional knock. The rate is index/s; accumulated damage sums rate × dt. A reduction needs its positive reference denominator. Differences between reduction percentages are percentage points, not a new reduction ratio.

viva.question: Is reward an independent sensor reading or a designed objective?
viva.short: It is designed from environment quantities, reference and preference weights.
viva.technical: engine_env.py:934–946 combines r_resp, r_fuel and r_life with actual obs_in[20:23] weights and uncertainty/smoothness penalties. It is not a best-action label or independent validation. Constraint costs are diagnostics and must not be subtracted again. Missing penalties imply partial decomposition; the total stays frame.reward.

viva.question: How do you distinguish a stable gain from choosing the best seed?
viva.short: Open Results, explain one selected pair, then compare all training pairs and the group confidence interval.
viva.technical: Training seeds can change learned weights. Evaluation uses frozen road seeds 1000–1019 and deterministic policy inference. The group interval includes zero: inconclusive does not prove no effect. Replaying exported weights is not the identical scored historical artifact. Source: results/agents/terrain_dt1/index.json; evaluate.py:134–154,298.

derived.note: Parameters derived from the car’s logs. This data fingerprint is not the same as the simulator-code plant fingerprint.

limitations: The 20 terrain_dt1 agents were trained on the pre-merge derived plant; their configs have git_dirty=true and data_sha1 but no plant_sha.
The knock model is unvalidated; spark advance accounts for much of the learned agents’ apparent gain over hand-written policies.
The turbine thermal node is modelled from assumed constants and cannot be checked against a vehicle turbine-temperature sensor.
At dt=1 s the block/coolant node oscillates; do not quote H/tau sweep results until the agreed integrator correction is made.
The damage integral is a simulation proxy, not a measured component lifetime prediction.
The current preview experiment is inconclusive; no claim of zero effect or a universal H/tau law is supported.
Exported policy.npz files are not exact scored Stable-Baselines3 final.zip files; any actor replay is an educational, UNVERIFIED rerun.
